teaching_language.majors_language: No formally named majors/tracks. The programme page lists the study plan under a single English flag (🇬🇧 Study Plan) with a Year II customisation of two elective courses. Unlike Marketing, Strategic Management, Administration Finance and Control, and Government and Public Affairs (which have separate Italian and English tracks), Global Management and Politics appears only once, in the 'Courses taught in English' column of every admission-route programme list.

campus: Rome, Italy (Luiss Guido Carli). The programme page does not name a specific campus building; Luiss headquarters is Viale Pola 12, 00198 Rome, and the Admissions Office is at Viale Romania 32, 00197 Rome.

admission_type.test_or_certification: Luiss admission Test, taken in Italian or English. Taking the Test in English gives access to both Italian-taught and English-taught programmes; taking it in Italian gives access only to Italian-taught programmes (so the English Test is required for Global Management and Politics). Rankings per first-choice course, out of 100, with a minimum admission threshold set per course by the Commission. English level B2 is assessed during the admission test.
admission_type.number_of_choices_allowed: Up to two master's degree courses, but both must be within the same subject area (Economics OR Law/Political Science)
admission_type.subject_area_group: Both - Global Management and Politics is listed in BOTH the Economics group and the Law/Political Science group on the 2027/2028 Luiss Test page, so it can be paired as a second choice with either an Economics programme or a Law/Political Science programme

admission_type.route_name: Direct admission with certifications (GMAT/GRE) - EU/Schengen students
admission_type.test_or_certification: GMAT with a minimum score of 515 (out of 805), OR GRE with a minimum score of 154 (out of 170) in BOTH the Verbal and Quantitative sections. Applicants attach the certificate and authorise Luiss to receive the official score via gmac.com / mba.com (GMAT) or ets.org (GRE); an unofficial score may be attached at application time. Admission is direct, based on the certification, subject to Committee review and available places. Submitting GMAT/GRE is one of the ways the required B2 English level is verified.
admission_type.subject_area_group: Both - Global Management and Politics is listed under both the Economics and the Law/Political Science headings, but only one programme may be selected and the choice is binding

admission_type.test_or_certification: Luiss admission Test, conducted online and remotely, in Italian or English (English required for English-taught programmes such as Global Management and Politics). Rankings per first-choice course out of 100 with a per-course minimum threshold; candidates who took the Graduate Summer School Admission Test receive an additional score. English level B2 is assessed during the admission test.
admission_type.number_of_choices_allowed: Up to two master's degree programmes in order of preference, within the same subject area (Economics or Law/Political Science)
admission_type.subject_area_group: Both - Global Management and Politics appears under both the Economics and the Political Science headings on the non-EU admission test page

admission_type.test_or_certification: GMAT with a minimum score of 515 (out of 805), OR GRE with a minimum score of 154 (out of 170) in the Quantitative and Verbal sections. Explicitly open to all master's programmes EXCEPT Finance and Management. Official score must be released to Luiss via gmac.com / mba.com or ets.org.
admission_type.subject_area_group: Both - listed under Economics and under Law/Political Science, but only one binding choice is permitted

academic_requirements.prior_qualification: A three-year bachelor's degree (Italian or foreign) that qualifies the holder for enrolment in an Italian master's degree programme. The degree may already be held or be obtained by 18 November 2027 for the 2027/2028 cycle.
academic_requirements.minimum_curricular_requirements: Per the Luiss 'Minimum curricular requirements' page, section 'Minimum academic requirements for admission to the selection process for the 2027/2028 academic year', Master's Degree in Global Management and Politics: admission is open to students enrolled in or graduates of L-18 (DM 270/04) / 17 (DM 509/99) Economics and Business Management; L-33 (DM 270/04) / 28 (DM 509/99) Economics; L-36 (DM 270/04) / 15 (DM 509/99) Political Science and International Relations. Students from other degree programmes may only be admitted if they have at least 24 university credits in total (earned or still to be earned) in at least three of the following subject areas: Business (ECON-06/A; ECON-07/A; ECON-08/A; ECON-09/A; ECON-09/B); Economics (ECON-01/A; ECON-04/A); Statistics (STAT-01/A; STAT-02/A; STAT-03/A; STAT-04/A; MATH-03/A; MATH-03/B); Law (GIUR-01/A; GIUR-02/A; GIUR-03/A; GIUR-05/A; GIUR-06/A; GIUR-09/A; GIUR-10/A). Note: the L-36 Political Science and International Relations class is accepted for this programme, which distinguishes it from the pure Economics masters (Management, Finance, Strategic Management, Marketing, AFC) that accept only L-18 and L-33. Requirements can only be satisfied by earning university credits (CFU) by the stated deadline; work experience and internships are not counted, and students transferring from another university may not make up missing requirements at Luiss.
academic_requirements.country_specific_rules: Foreign qualifications must have been awarded on completion of a first-level programme of at least 3 (or 4) academic years, must entitle the holder to enrol in graduate programmes in the awarding country, and must be issued by an official university in that country's education system. Professional/vocational qualifications are not eligible for Italian 'Laurea Magistrale' admission (only for 'Master di primo livello'). Where a system offers both Ordinary and Honours Bachelor's degrees, only Honours Bachelor's degrees qualify.
academic_requirements.document_recognition: Depends on country group: (a) Lisbon Recognition Convention signatory countries - Diploma Supplement may be submitted; (b) countries in the ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database - Italy) - CIMEA Statement of Verification or an Apostille of the diploma issued via the competent Italian Embassy/Consulate; (c) countries not in ARDI or the Lisbon Convention - CIMEA Statement of Comparability or a Declaration of Value (DoV) from the competent Italian Embassy/Consulate. Enrolment is always subject to verification of validity by the Luiss Admissions Office.
academic_requirements.compensatory_measures: If minimum curricular requirements are not met at application time, the candidate must submit - by the admission application deadline - documentation proving they will meet them by the cycle's degree/credit deadline (9 November 2026 for the closed 2026/2027 cycle; the equivalent 2027/2028 date is 18 November 2027 per the selection calendars). Requirements may only be satisfied with university credits (CFU), not work experience or internships. No foundation-year or other compensatory pathway is documented for this master's programme.

language_requirements.assessed_in_test: Yes. The minimum curricular requirements page states for Global Management and Politics: 'In addition, students must have at least a B2 level of English, which will be assessed during the admission test.' The same page adds that, depending on the admission route, B2 proficiency is verified 'for example, by passing the Admission Test in English or by submitting GMAT or GRE certificates.'
language_requirements.exemptions: Not stated on the official pages consulted. In practice the two documented verification methods are (1) passing the Luiss Admission Test taken in English, or (2) submitting a qualifying GMAT or GRE certificate on the direct-admission route.

tuition_or_fees_link.annual_amount: EUR 15,000.00 per year according to the official programme page for 2027/2028: 'The annual single tuition fee for enrolment in the Master's Degree Programme in Global Management and Politics is € 15,000.00, divided into 3 instalments, plus the regional student welfare tax.' Global Management and Politics is therefore NOT in the EUR 18,000 Management/Finance bracket, but the programme page (EUR 15,000) and the admission FAQ (EUR 16,000) disagree.

uncertainty_notes: ACADEMIC YEAR: The programme page carries the badge 'Year 2027/2028' and all four admission pages publish the 2027/2028 calendar, so 2027/2028 is the primary cycle. However, the admission pages still sit under URL slugs containing '20262027' and Luiss explicitly states the full 2027/2028 Admission Notice 'will be published from November 2026'. Cycle status is therefore 'notice not yet published' - all dates recorded here come from the published selection calendar, not from a signed bando. The 2026/2027 cycle is closed (degree/curricular requirements had to be met by 9 November 2026).

LUISS TEST SUBJECT AREA - RESOLVED BUT DUAL: 'Global Management and Politics' is listed in BOTH the Economics column AND the Law/Political Science column on the EU Luiss Test page, the EU GMAT/GRE page, the non-EU test page and the non-EU certified selection page. This means the two-choice rule can be satisfied by pairing it with either an Economics or a Law/Political Science programme. Luiss does not state this dual listing as an explicit rule anywhere - it is inferred from the programme appearing twice in the same tables - so an applicant should confirm with ammissione@luiss.it before relying on a cross-area pairing.

FINANCE/MANAGEMENT EXCLUSION DOES NOT APPLY: Despite 'Management' in its name, Global Management and Politics is NOT subject to the Finance/Management exclusion. It is explicitly listed among the programmes available via the Luiss Test (EU and non-EU) and via the GMAT/GRE routes, whereas Finance and Management are absent from every list and have their own separate selection page.

TUITION CONFLICT: The official programme page states EUR 15,000.00 per year for Global Management and Politics, but the FAQ block repeated on all four master's admission pages states 'The one-off annual fee is €16,000 for the first year and €18,000 for the Bachelor's degree programmes in Management and Finance.' The EUR 18,000 Management/Finance bracket clearly does not apply here, but EUR 15,000 vs EUR 16,000 is an unresolved contradiction between the programme page and the admission FAQ. The FAQ wording itself is garbled (it says 'Bachelor's degree programmes' on a master's page). Recommend treating EUR 15,000 as the programme-specific figure and flagging the discrepancy.
